answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer:
No, and I would not want you to try. You are 20 days from the start line, which is squarely in taper territory. A 22-miler now would leave you flat on race day, with no fitness gain to show for it.

Here is what you actually have in the bank: a 20-miler three weeks ago, a 17 last week at 9:59/mi with only +4.7 bpm of drift, and five straight weeks of consistent 40 to 53 mi. That is enough to finish a marathon well under 3:45. The job now is to arrive fresh, not to add one more number.

Trust the taper. The one dress-rehearsal piece you still get is Wednesday's 4 mi at marathon pace and Sunday's last 3 at marathon pace, so you lock in the feel of 8:35/mi.

new.analysis:
You followed the plan to the mile last week: all five runs done, long run on target at 17 mi, threshold hit at 3 x 2 mi right around 7:58/mi. That is exactly the kind of execution that earns a good taper.

The signals are green. Easy pace sits at 9:50/mi at 138 bpm, drift on the long run was small, and no pain reported anywhere. The threshold work landed at the right place too, with 47% of time in zone 4 and heart rate climbing cleanly as the reps went on.

Because the race moved up two weeks, I am treating this as the first taper week rather than another build week. Volume comes down from 42 to about 37 mi, the quality session shortens to a marathon-pace rehearsal instead of threshold, and the long run drops to 14 with race-pace work at the end. The following week will cut further, and race week is almost all shakeout.

On the shoes: the Ghost 16 is at 149 mi and the Endorphin Speed 4 at 56. If you are racing in the Endorphins, do Wednesday's marathon-pace block in them so there are no surprises. If not, race in the pair your legs know.

Anxiety about the new date is normal and does not change the plan. The best antidote is doing the easy days easy, nailing the two sharpening sessions, and sleeping. Water, food and a race-day plan are the next conversation.
